prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Conroe, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1076; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers responded to a two-vehicle collision in Conroef, Texas, where Driver 1 and Driver 2 were operating vehicles that came together in a low-speed head-on impact. Driver 1 reported neck strain at the scene and was evaluated by responding personnel. The reported injury is consistent with the mechanics of a collision of this type. Driver 1 was seated in the vehicle at the time of impact, and this was confirmed by the investigating officer, by independent witnesses at the scene, and by Driver 2. Witness statements, scene photographs, and Driver 2's account all agree on the sequence of events as described. No prior damage to Driver 1's vehicle is known to officers or to any witness. Officers noted that it is not clear whether all of the visible damage resulted from this impact, and the extent of that damage will need further assessment by a qualified inspector. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle involved. A Passenger was also present in Driver 2's vehicle and was checked at the scene, with no injuries reported.
